text:
Connor McDavid arrives in Toronto with a 20-game point streak (11 goals, 38 assists) and the usual noise following him. "I was a Leafs fan as a kid," he said this week, by Sportskeeda's headline, and Culture Alberta ran his wife Lauren's answer to the Maple Leafs speculation: "We're Not Going to Toronto." Our numbers have him at 93% for a point and 71% for two or more. Zach Hyman, back where his NHL career started, is one point from 500.

The home side is in a much darker place. The Maple Leafs are winless in five (0-5-0), outscored 22-9, and every loss came at home. The chances say it's real: 41% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) over that stretch. Auston Matthews called out teammates after the Devils game (NDTV Sports), William Nylander is answering trade talk (TSN, Sportskeeda), and our playoff model gives Toronto a 4.6% chance. Kirill Marchenko (14 points in 14 games) is on injured reserve; since he went down, Jack Roslovic has moved onto the first power play and has 14 points in his last 10. The one bright memory: Toronto won the first meeting 7-2 on Oct 24.

Edmonton is winning, though not always on merit. Mike Babcock's Oilers have won three straight, 10-5, with 47% of the expected goals and their goaltending saving 3.8 goals above expected. Devon Levi, our projected starter and a headline all week in Edmonton, is at +1.5 this season. Anthony Stolarz is confirmed for Toronto (The Leafs Nation reported it), starting over Sergei Bobrovsky, who has 13 of 21 starts.

Our sleeper is Colton Dach, a third-liner at about 15:17 a night whose shots have been dangerous: 2.1 expected goals in his last 10 games, better than 72% of depth forwards, with four from high-danger spots, against a Leafs team that allows the 7th-most expected goals per 60. We have him at 16% to score and 30% for a point.
headline: McDavid's streak meets a Leafs team in freefall
